title: Circuit Builder: Light It Up!
description: Build a working electrical circuit by dragging and dropping the right components into the correct slots! Place a battery, wires, switch, LED, resistor, and buzzer in the proper positions to complete a functioning circuit. Learn how electricity flows and why each component matters.
learning_objectives: Understand the basic components of an electrical circuit and their functions
Learn how electric current flows in a closed circuit from the power source through each component
Recognise the role of a resistor in protecting components by limiting current flow
Understand the purpose of a switch as a circuit breaker that controls the flow of electricity
Connect physics theory (Ohm's Law, series circuits) to hands-on circuit building

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Read the description of each empty slot on the circuit board -- it tells you what kind of component belongs there
Drag a component from the parts tray and drop it into the slot you think is correct
If you place the correct component, the slot lights up green and you earn points
If the component is wrong, you get an error message and a hint -- try again with a different piece
Place all 6 components correctly within the 2-minute time limit to complete the circuit and make the LED glow and the buzzer ring!
After completing the circuit, read the explanation to understand how current flows through your completed circuit
tips: Start with what you are most sure about -- the battery (power source) is usually the easiest to place first
Think about the flow of electricity: it must go from the battery, through a switch, through a resistor, to the output devices (LED and buzzer), and back
Use the hints if you get stuck -- there is no penalty for reading hints, only for incorrect placements

minigame_config.description: Build a basic electrical circuit by placing components in the correct slots. Arrange a battery, connecting wire, switch, resistor, LED, and buzzer to create a working series circuit.

pieces.label: Battery (9V)
pieces.description: A 9-volt battery that serves as the power source. It creates a potential difference (voltage) that pushes electrons through the circuit.

pieces.label: Connecting Wire
pieces.description: A copper conducting wire that connects components together, providing a path for electric current to flow through the circuit.

pieces.label: Toggle Switch
pieces.description: A toggle switch that can open or close the circuit. When ON, current flows; when OFF, the circuit is broken and no current flows.

pieces.label: LED (Light Emitting Diode)
pieces.description: A Light Emitting Diode that glows when current passes through it. LEDs are energy-efficient and used in everything from indicator lights to home bulbs.

pieces.label: Resistor (220Ω)
pieces.description: A 220-ohm resistor that limits the amount of current flowing through the circuit. Without it, excess current could burn out the LED or buzzer.

pieces.label: Piezo Buzzer
pieces.description: A piezoelectric buzzer that produces a tone when electric current passes through it. Used in doorbells, alarms, and timer circuits across India.

slots.label: Power Source
slots.hint: Every circuit needs a source of electrical energy. What component creates the voltage that pushes electrons through the circuit?
slots.success_message: Correct! The 9V battery provides the electromotive force (EMF) that drives current through the entire circuit.
slots.error_message: That is not a power source. The power source must generate voltage to push electrons -- think about what provides electrical energy.

slots.label: Conductor Path
slots.hint: Current needs a path to travel from one component to the next. What provides a conductive pathway in a circuit?
slots.success_message: Correct! The copper wire acts as a conductor, allowing electrons to flow freely between components with minimal resistance.
slots.error_message: That component does not serve as a conductor. You need something that provides a continuous conductive path for electrons to travel through.

slots.label: Circuit Control
slots.hint: You need a way to turn the circuit ON and OFF without disconnecting wires. What component controls whether current flows?
slots.success_message: Correct! The toggle switch controls the circuit. When closed (ON), the circuit is complete and current flows. When open (OFF), the circuit breaks.
slots.error_message: That is not a control device. Think about what allows you to open and close the circuit -- to turn it on and off at will.

slots.label: Current Limiter
slots.hint: Without this component, too much current would flow and could damage the LED and buzzer. What limits current in a circuit? (Hint: Ohm's Law -- V = IR)
slots.success_message: Correct! The 220-ohm resistor limits current to a safe level. Using Ohm's Law (I = V/R), it ensures the LED and buzzer receive the right amount of current.
slots.error_message: That component does not limit current. You need something that provides resistance to control how much current flows -- think about Ohm's Law.

slots.label: Light Output
slots.hint: This slot needs a component that converts electrical energy into visible light. What semiconductor device emits light when current passes through it?
slots.success_message: Correct! The LED converts electrical energy into light. LEDs are used widely in India -- from traffic signals in Delhi to decorative Diwali lights!
slots.error_message: That component does not produce light. You need a semiconductor device specifically designed to emit visible light when forward-biased.

slots.label: Sound Output
slots.hint: This slot needs a component that converts electrical energy into sound. What device produces an audible tone when current flows through it?
slots.success_message: Correct! The piezo buzzer converts electrical energy into sound waves. Buzzers are found in Indian households in doorbells, pressure cooker timers, and alarm clocks!
slots.error_message: That component does not produce sound. You need a device that vibrates to create audible sound when electric current passes through it.

minigame_config.circuit_explanation: In your completed series circuit, current flows from the positive terminal of the 9V battery, through the connecting wire to the toggle switch. When the switch is ON, current continues through the 220-ohm resistor (which limits current to protect the components), then through the LED (which glows), then through the piezo buzzer (which rings), and finally back to the negative terminal of the battery. This is how Ohm's Law (V = IR) works in practice -- the battery provides 9V, the resistor controls the current, and energy is converted into light and sound.

glossary_terms.definition: A closed loop or pathway through which electric current flows. A basic circuit requires a power source (battery), conductors (wires), a load (LED, buzzer), and optionally a switch for control.
glossary_terms.example: A simple torch (flashlight) is a circuit: battery provides power, wires connect the components, and the bulb is the load that converts electrical energy to light.

glossary_terms.definition: A fundamental law of electricity stating that the current (I) through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage (V) across it and inversely proportional to the resistance (R). Formula: V = I x R.
glossary_terms.example: In this circuit, with a 9V battery and a 220-ohm resistor, the current is I = 9/220 = approximately 0.04 amperes (40 milliamps).

glossary_terms.definition: A passive electrical component that limits the flow of electric current in a circuit. Resistance is measured in ohms. Resistors protect sensitive components from receiving too much current.
glossary_terms.example: Without the 220-ohm resistor, the LED in our circuit would receive too much current from the 9V battery and burn out within seconds.

glossary_terms.definition: A semiconductor device that emits light when current flows through it in the forward direction. LEDs are energy-efficient, long-lasting, and used extensively in modern lighting and electronics.
glossary_terms.example: India's UJALA scheme distributed over 36 crore LED bulbs across the country, saving approximately 48 billion kWh of electricity annually.

win_conditions.description: Place all 6 circuit components in the correct slots within 2 minutes to build a working circuit! Fewer wrong placements = higher score. Complete the circuit to watch the LED glow and the buzzer ring!

coaching_moment: Notice how each decision here requires weighing multiple options. Strategic thinkers pause before choosing — what's the long-term implication of each answer?
cultural_context: Scientific literacy is a strategic priority under NEP 2020, which emphasises inquiry-based learning over rote memorisation. Circuit Builder: Light It Up! builds the analytical instincts that support strong performance in India's science curricula.
